explanation_en: This figurative expression is used to indicate that an action, comment, or thought is consistent with or similar to previous ones. It is very common in journalistic, academic, and professional Spanish. You can vary the demonstrative adjective (e.g., 'en esa misma línea', 'en la misma línea').

examples.en_text: The director proposed a new project and, along the same lines, suggested hiring more staff.
examples.target_text: El director propuso un nuevo proyecto y, en esta misma línea, sugirió contratar más personal.

examples.en_text: Many teachers think the exam is very difficult and, along these same lines, are asking to change the syllabus.
examples.target_text: Muchos profesores piensan que el examen es muy difícil y, en esta misma línea, piden cambiar el temario.

examples.en_text: We want to reduce plastic use in the office and, along the same lines, we are going to give away reusable bottles.
examples.target_text: Queremos reducir el uso de plástico en la oficina y, en esta misma línea, vamos a regalar botellas reutilizables.

examples.en_text: The government wants to improve public transport and, along the same lines, will lower the price of train tickets.
examples.target_text: El gobierno quiere mejorar el transporte público y, en esta misma línea, bajará el precio de los billetes de tren.

examples.en_text: His first novel was a mystery success and, along the same lines, his second book promises to maintain the suspense.
examples.target_text: Su primera novela fue un éxito de misterio y, en esta misma línea, su segundo libro promete mantener la intriga.

examples.en_text: To lead a healthy life it is important to exercise and, along these same lines, take care of your daily diet.
examples.target_text: Para llevar una vida sana es importante hacer ejercicio y, en esta misma línea, cuidar la alimentación diaria.

explanation_en: This is a very common connector used to introduce a contrasting point or an alternative perspective. It is equivalent to 'on the other hand' in English. It is highly useful for structuring arguments in both spoken and written Spanish.

examples.en_text: I love my current job; on the other hand, the salary could be better.
examples.target_text: Me encanta mi trabajo actual; por otro lado, el sueldo podría ser mejor.

examples.en_text: Traveling by train is very comfortable, but on the other hand, it takes much longer than the plane.
examples.target_text: Viajar en tren es muy cómodo, pero por otro lado, tarda mucho más que el avión.

examples.en_text: Living in the city center is convenient; on the other hand, the noise is sometimes unbearable.
examples.target_text: Vivir en el centro de la ciudad es conveniente; por otro lado, el ruido a veces es insoportable.

examples.en_text: Social media keeps us connected, but on the other hand, it can make us waste a lot of time.
examples.target_text: Las redes sociales nos mantienen conectados, pero por otro lado, pueden hacernos perder mucho tiempo.

examples.en_text: On one hand, I want to go to the beach, but on the other hand, it's going to rain all weekend.
examples.target_text: Por un lado, quiero ir a la playa, pero por otro lado, va a llover todo el fin de semana.

examples.en_text: The photography course seems very interesting; on the other hand, I don't know if I have enough time to do it.
examples.target_text: El curso de fotografía parece muy interesante; por otro lado, no sé si tengo suficiente tiempo para hacerlo.

explanation_en: 'Tener en cuenta' is a fundamental Spanish idiom meaning 'to take into account', 'to keep in mind', or 'to consider'. It is widely used in both spoken and written Spanish across all registers. It is often followed by 'que' and a clause.

examples.en_text: Let's bear in mind the budget before making a final decision.
examples.target_text: Tengamos en cuenta el presupuesto antes de tomar una decisión final.

examples.en_text: It is important that we bear in mind the region's weather for this trip.
examples.target_text: Es importante que tengamos en cuenta el clima de la región para este viaje.

examples.en_text: Let's bear in mind that the shops close early on Sundays.
examples.target_text: Tengamos en cuenta que las tiendas cierran temprano los domingos.

examples.en_text: When cooking, let's bear in mind the guests' allergies.
examples.target_text: Al cocinar, tengamos en cuenta las alergias de los invitados.

examples.en_text: For tomorrow's exam, let's bear in mind the teacher's advice.
examples.target_text: Para el examen de mañana, tengamos en cuenta los consejos del profesor.

examples.en_text: Although we may not agree, let's bear in mind his point of view.
examples.target_text: Aunque no estemos de acuerdo, tengamos en cuenta su punto de vista.

explanation_en: A figurative expression used to describe a situation that is highly likely to cause major problems or explode into a crisis in the future. It is used in both informal and formal contexts, such as politics, economics, and social issues, to warn of impending danger.

examples.en_text: Working fifteen hours a day without resting is a time bomb for your health.
examples.target_text: Trabajar quince horas al día sin descansar es una bomba de tiempo para tu salud.

examples.en_text: Their relationship is a time bomb; they argue about everything and can't stand each other anymore.
examples.target_text: Su relación es una bomba de tiempo; discuten por todo y ya no se soportan.

examples.en_text: The city's old bridge is a time bomb and needs urgent repairs.
examples.target_text: El viejo puente de la ciudad es una bomba de tiempo y necesita reparaciones urgentes.

examples.en_text: That company's debt is a time bomb that could explode at any moment.
examples.target_text: La deuda de esa empresa es una bomba de tiempo que podría estallar en cualquier momento.

examples.en_text: Not fixing these software errors now is a time bomb for the future of the project.
examples.target_text: No corregir estos errores de software ahora es una bomba de tiempo para el futuro del proyecto.

examples.en_text: The lack of employment among young people is a time bomb for the country's economy.
examples.target_text: La falta de empleo entre los jóvenes es una bomba de tiempo para la economía del país.

explanation_en: Unlike English, which has a single verb 'to borrow', Spanish uses the verbal collocation 'pedir prestado' (literally 'to ask for lent'). It is the standard way to express borrowing money, objects, or resources, and is essential for natural communication.

examples.en_text: You are always borrowing money from your parents and it's about time you look for a job.
examples.target_text: Siempre estás pidiendo prestado dinero a tus padres y ya es hora de que busques un trabajo.

examples.en_text: I prefer to borrow this book from the library before buying it.
examples.target_text: Prefiero pedir prestado este libro en la biblioteca antes de comprarlo.

examples.en_text: My brother borrowed my car to go to his job interview.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano me pidió prestado el coche para ir a su entrevista de trabajo.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I saw Laura borrowing a bit of sugar from the neighbor.
examples.target_text: Ayer vi a Laura pidiendo prestado un poco de azúcar a la vecina.

examples.en_text: She didn't want to spend money, so she ended up borrowing her sister's dress.
examples.target_text: Ella no quería gastar dinero, así que terminó pidiendo prestado el vestido de su hermana.

examples.en_text: Juan always forgets to bring a pen and borrows one from his classmate.
examples.target_text: Juan siempre se olvida de traer un bolígrafo y le pide prestado uno a su compañero.

explanation_en: While 'arrastrar' literally means 'to drag' physically, in figurative and professional contexts, it means to carry over or continue to suffer from long-standing problems, debts, or challenges. It highlights that these issues are heavy burdens from the past that have not been resolved.

examples.en_text: Even though the suitcase is broken, he continues to drag it all over the airport.
examples.target_text: A pesar de que la maleta está rota, él la sigue arrastrando por todo el aeropuerto.

examples.en_text: Juan is still carrying that knee injury from last year and cannot play well.
examples.target_text: Juan sigue arrastrando esa lesión de rodilla desde el año pasado y no puede jugar bien.

examples.en_text: We are still dragging along the debts we accumulated during the crisis.
examples.target_text: Todavía seguimos arrastrando las deudas que acumulamos durante la crisis.

examples.en_text: You are not going to be happy if you keep dragging along the mistakes of your past.
examples.target_text: No vas a ser feliz si sigues arrastrando los errores de tu pasado.

examples.en_text: Many local businesses continue to drag along the effects of the pandemic.
examples.target_text: Muchos negocios locales siguen arrastrando los efectos de la pandemia.

examples.en_text: The dog keeps dragging his blanket all over the house because he wants to play.
examples.target_text: El perro sigue arrastrando su manta por toda la casa porque quiere jugar.

explanation_en: This phrase means to remain standing, either physically (due to exhaustion or illness) or metaphorically (staying strong during a crisis). It is a pronominal verb construction ('mantenerse') followed by the prepositional phrase 'en pie'. Learners should note that 'en pie' is fixed and does not change to plural or feminine (e.g., 'ellas se mantienen en pie').

examples.en_text: I am so tired after the trip that I can barely stay on my feet.
examples.target_text: Estoy tan cansado después del viaje que apenas puedo mantenerme en pie.

examples.en_text: You have to eat a good breakfast if you want to stay on your feet during the concert.
examples.target_text: Tienes que desayunar bien si quieres mantenerte en pie durante el concierto.

examples.en_text: Despite the strong wind, the tent managed to stay standing.
examples.target_text: A pesar del fuerte viento, la tienda de campaña logró mantenerse en pie.

examples.en_text: We worked twelve hours straight and at the end of the day we could no longer stay on our feet.
examples.target_text: Trabajamos doce horas seguidas y al final del día ya no podíamos mantenernos en pie.

examples.en_text: With this high fever, I find it impossible to stay on my feet.
examples.target_text: Con esta fiebre tan alta, me resulta imposible mantenerme en pie.

examples.en_text: The bus passengers were trying to stay on their feet during the sharp turns.
examples.target_text: Los pasajeros del autobús intentaban mantenerse en pie durante las curvas cerradas.

explanation_en: This expression is used to steer a conversation or debate away from speculation, emotions, or opinions and focus on objective reality. It is highly common in debates, journalism, and formal discussions. The preposition 'a' is crucial here, indicating movement or transition towards the concrete evidence.

examples.en_text: I don't want any more opinions about the project; let's look at the facts and look at the numbers.
examples.target_text: No quiero más opiniones sobre el proyecto; vamos a los hechos y miremos los números.

examples.en_text: There are many rumors in the office, but let's get to the facts: no one has lost their job yet.
examples.target_text: Hay muchos rumores en la oficina, pero vamos a los hechos: nadie ha perdido su trabajo todavía.

examples.en_text: Before making a final decision, let's look at the facts of what really happened yesterday.
examples.target_text: Antes de tomar una decisión final, vayamos a los hechos de lo que realmente pasó ayer.

examples.en_text: Let's put the excuses aside and look at the facts to solve this problem quickly.
examples.target_text: Dejemos las excusas a un lado y vamos a los hechos para resolver este problema rápido.

examples.en_text: If we look at the facts, the economy has improved a bit this month, even if it doesn't seem like it.
examples.target_text: Si vamos a los hechos, la economía ha mejorado un poco este mes, aunque no lo parezca.

examples.en_text: Don't get angry with me; let's look at the facts and talk about what we can prove.
examples.target_text: No te enfades conmigo; vamos a los hechos y hablemos de lo que podemos demostrar.

explanation_en: This is a key socio-political term in Spanish, particularly in discussions about immigration, referring to policies or conditions that attract migrants (a 'pull factor'). It consists of the noun 'efecto' followed directly by 'llamada' (call) acting as an adjective. It is almost always used with the verbs 'provocar', 'causar', or 'producir'.

examples.en_text: Some politicians fear that giving financial aid without control will create a pull factor.
examples.target_text: Algunos políticos temen que dar ayudas económicas sin control genere un efecto llamada.

examples.en_text: The photos of that beach on social media have created an incredible magnet effect this summer.
examples.target_text: Las fotos de esa playa en las redes sociales han creado un efecto llamada increíble este verano.

examples.en_text: High salaries in the tech sector act as a pull factor for young professionals.
examples.target_text: Los altos salarios en el sector tecnológico actúan como un efecto llamada para los jóvenes profesionales.

examples.en_text: Lowering rent prices in this area could produce a magnet effect for new tenants.
examples.target_text: Bajar el precio del alquiler en esta zona podría producir un efecto llamada de nuevos inquilinos.

examples.en_text: The prestige of this university has a major pull factor for foreign students.
examples.target_text: El prestigio de esta universidad tiene un gran efecto llamada para los estudiantes extranjeros.

examples.en_text: Reducing taxes on startups can trigger a magnet effect for investors.
examples.target_text: Reducir los impuestos a las nuevas empresas puede provocar un efecto llamada de inversores.

explanation_en: This expression means to evaluate a situation, weighing the positives and negatives, much like balancing a financial ledger. It is widely used in business, politics, and personal reflection at the end of a period or event. A common pitfall is translating 'to take stock' literally instead of using this idiomatic equivalent.

examples.en_text: At the end of the year, stock will be taken of everything we have achieved in the company.
examples.target_text: Al final del año, se hará balance de todo lo que hemos logrado en la empresa.

examples.en_text: Once the election campaign is over, an assessment will be made of the results.
examples.target_text: Una vez que termine la campaña electoral, se hará balance de los resultados.

examples.en_text: In tomorrow's meeting, stock will be taken of the losses and profits of the quarter.
examples.target_text: En la reunión de mañana se hará balance de las pérdidas y ganancias del trimestre.

examples.en_text: After the crisis, stock has been taken of the damage and we are now ready to continue.
examples.target_text: Después de la crisis, se ha hecho balance de los daños y ya estamos listos para continuar.

examples.en_text: When this very long project ends, an assessment will be made as to whether the effort was really worth it.
examples.target_text: Cuando termine este proyecto tan largo, se hará balance de si realmente valió la pena el esfuerzo.

examples.en_text: At the end of the tourist season, stock is always taken of the local economic situation.
examples.target_text: Al terminar la temporada de turismo, siempre se hace balance de la situación económica local.

explanation_en: While it can be used literally in medicine, this phrase is very frequently used metaphorically to mean resolving conflicts, moving past grievances, or reconciling after a dispute. It is a common collocation in political discourse and personal relationships. Note that Spanish uses the definite article 'las heridas' rather than possessive pronouns when the context makes the owner clear.

examples.en_text: After many years of arguments, the family finally managed to heal the wounds of the past.
examples.target_text: Después de muchos años de discusiones, la familia finalmente logró cerrar las heridas del pasado.

examples.en_text: Time helps to heal wounds, but sometimes the process is very slow.
examples.target_text: El tiempo ayuda a cerrar las heridas, pero a veces el proceso es muy lento.

examples.en_text: The new president promised to work to heal the wounds of society after the crisis.
examples.target_text: El nuevo presidente prometió trabajar para cerrar las heridas de la sociedad tras la crisis.

examples.en_text: I am still healing the wounds from my last relationship, so I don't want to date anyone right now.
examples.target_text: Todavía estoy cerrando las heridas de mi última relación, así que no quiero salir con nadie ahora.

examples.en_text: A sincere apology was enough to heal the wounds between the two friends.
examples.target_text: Una disculpa sincera fue suficiente para cerrar las heridas entre los dos amigos.

examples.en_text: It is important to talk about what happened so that the wounds heal completely.
examples.target_text: Es importante hablar de lo que pasó para que las heridas se cierren por completo.

explanation_en: This term is widely used in journalism to refer to the main location or subject of news coverage at a given moment. It combines 'foco' (focus or spotlight) with 'informativo' (informative or news-related). It is highly common in news broadcasts and written press.

examples.en_text: After the floods, the small town became the country's main focus of media attention.
examples.target_text: Tras las inundaciones, el pequeño pueblo se convirtió en el principal foco informativo del país.

examples.en_text: The economy minister's press conference is today's major focus of media attention.
examples.target_text: La rueda de prensa de la ministra de economía es hoy el gran foco informativo.

examples.en_text: The signing of the star player has been the focus of media attention all week.
examples.target_text: El fichaje del jugador estrella ha sido el foco informativo durante toda la semana.

examples.en_text: With the presentation of the new phone, the tech company is once again in the media spotlight.
examples.target_text: Con la presentación del nuevo teléfono, la empresa tecnológica vuelve a estar en el foco informativo.

examples.en_text: During the film festival, the city transforms into an international focus of media attention.
examples.target_text: Durante el festival de cine, la ciudad se transforma en un foco informativo internacional.

examples.en_text: The transport strike has shifted the focus of media attention toward supply issues.
examples.target_text: La huelga de transportes ha desplazado el foco informativo hacia los problemas de suministro.
